sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2015. Request for Change to ISO 639-3 Language Code, Change Request Number 2015-047: retire [btl] Bhatola (non-existent). Submitted 2015-06-16 by Editor, Ethnologue (SIL International); adopted 2016-01-15. 5 pp.
sources.note: Nothing; administrative retirement record. p. 2, sec. 3(c): 'Shukla (1986:22) says that Bhatola does not exist. This language does not appear in the listing of Scheduled Tribes (Singh 1997). The Ethnologue has no information on the language, reporting that it is unclassified. Hammarstrom (2015) agrees with the assessment that the language does not exist.'

sources.citation: Lewis, M. Paul, Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2014. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 17th edn. Dallas: SIL International. Entry 'Bhatola' [btl] (Internet Archive copy 2014-09-25).
sources.note: Nothing. Entry reads: India, ISO 639-3 btl, population 5,050 (2000), Madhya Pradesh, status 6a (Vigorous), classification Unclassified, 'Bhatola is a subgroup of the Gond Scheduled Tribe in Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Chhattisgarh.' No linguistic data, no sources.

Nothing. Entry retired, 'kept for administrative purposes'; retired in ISO 639-3 via CR 2015-047 (2016-01-15), reason non-existent; no descriptive references (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology).
